items.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: Cedar Walton, Reggie Workman, Freddie Hubbard and Curtis Fuller went with that group.

ctx.x: What was the name of the place?

The Sloan House YMCA. 34th Street between Eighth and Ninth Avenue. Because I had five thousand dollars when I got there. In 1959 five thousand dollars was probably like what, 20 or 30 thousand dollars, because the cost of living was down. I mean Transcontinental Airlines from New York to Chicago by [Inaudible] was 24 dollars and 50 cents. The Four Seasons, the Sheraton, the Waldorf was like 50 dollars a week. You go there now, the occupancy rate is 65 dollars a night. That’s aside from the 300 or 499 dollars, you…

month, which wasn’t bad. Now I’m sure that same place — I go by there sometimes and look at the building — I’m sure that place probably rents for five thousand dollars a month. The same place. So I said I need a phone, so I called the phone company. First thing, “Do you have any references?” I said, “Yeah I play with Lionel Hampton’s Orchestra. They checked it out, telephone, no problem. So the gig worked that way. So now we’re getting ready to go to Wildwood, New Jersey. So Cedar Walton, one of my dearest…
